Arab nationalism. This political and cultural movement emerged in the late nineteenth century as an intellectual response to Ottoman Empire rule, enabled by printing presses and journalism. It gained momentum after World War One with the empire's collapse and the arbitrary borders of Sykes-Picot. Gamal Abdel Nasser embodied its peak with the nineteen fifty-two Egyptian Revolution, nationalization of the Suez Canal, and dreams of pan-Arab union, though it fractured later through inter-Arab rivalries and Cold War alignments.
